scope: Fixed-source static native API contract delta; no model/native/JNI/device execution and no network fetch.

contracts.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_init_context(libusb_context **ctx, const struct libusb_init_option options[], int num_options);
contracts.owner: Adapter owns the explicitly returned context until libusb_exit; libuvc will only borrow it.
contracts.blocking: Initialisation and internal locks; no documented end-to-end deadline.
contracts.return_codes: 0: output context valid; negative LIBUSB_ERROR: output not valid.
contracts.callback_last_reference: No adapter transfer callback registered by this API; context must outlive all future calls/callbacks.
conditions: Use non-NULL output ctx and exactly one NO_DEVICE_DISCOVERY init option on the new context.
Do not rely on options being applied when reusing a default context.
NO_DEVICE_DISCOVERY disables Linux scan/hotplug, not Android permission enforcement.
limitations: Does not prove USB ioctl access or device support.
libusb_set_option(NULL,...) affects later contexts and is not equivalent isolation.

contains: Hotplug functionality will also be deactivated.
This option should only be used with libusb_init_context()

contracts.conclusion: New precision: init-time option and default-context reuse semantics are binding; Android hotplug must be owned outside this disabled discovery path.

contracts.owner: Adapter owns libusb_context; libuvc owns its uvc_context allocation but does not take ownership of supplied USB context.
contracts.return_codes: UVC_SUCCESS or initialisation error; this fixed code has an unchecked calloc before dereference.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Caller supplies and keeps event processing alive when usb_ctx is supplied.
conditions: Pass the already initialised dedicated USB context.
Keep USB context alive through all UVC calls and uvc_exit.
limitations: uvc_init(NULL USB ctx) takes a different ownership path and uses legacy libusb_init.
OOM path is not shown to cleanly return error for every allocation.
contracts.conclusion: Borrowed context means no libuvc-owned event thread; lifecycle adapter must own the pump.

contracts.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_wrap_sys_device(libusb_context *ctx, intptr_t sys_dev, libusb_device_handle **dev_handle);
contracts.owner: Android connection/explicit FD owner retains original fd; libusb owns wrapper handle, borrows fd.
contracts.blocking: Documented non-blocking/no bus requests; allocation, locks and Linux ioctl/backend work still exist, no hard deadline proof.
contracts.return_codes: 0: output handle valid; NO_MEM, ACCESS, NOT_SUPPORTED or other LIBUSB_ERROR on failure.
contracts.callback_last_reference: The borrowed original fd must stay open until wrapper close and all authorised users have returned.
conditions: One owner closes original fd after native release.
Do not reopen the temporary libusb_device using libusb_open.
Bind fd to immutable session identity, not its numeric reuse alone.
limitations: Linux backend stores fd directly and sets fd_keep; no dup ownership transfer is performed here.
Permission and live attachment must be established externally.

contains: will not be closed by libusb_close()
shall not be opened through libusb_open()

contracts.conclusion: Inherited FD ownership contract confirmed at implementation level.

contracts.owner: libuvc owns its internal libusb wrapper/device handle; caller retains original fd and UVC context.
contracts.blocking: Not merely fd wrapping: descriptor access, interface claim and status transfer submission occur before return; no bounded open/cancellation API exposed.
contracts.return_codes: Propagates wrap/open errors; success assigns *devh at end of uvc_open_internal.
contracts.callback_last_reference: A status transfer can be submitted while open is still executing; independently running event processing can act before outer open returns.
conditions: Do not call libusb_wrap_sys_device separately then pass its pointer as fd.
Hold open-call/session references before entering uvc_wrap; do not free context/FD while open returns late.
Only consume output devh on successful return.
limitations: Header exposes this API only when LIBUSB_API_VERSION >= 0x01000107.
This static analysis does not establish a cancellation-safe public uvc_wrap implementation.
Internal allocation/status cleanup gaps from prior report remain.
contracts.conclusion: New precision: public open can register asynchronous status work before publishing its returned handle; an atomic model open is insufficient evidence.

contracts.owner: Transfer/buffer/user_data owner must establish operation identity and adapter call reference before submission; successful submission adds a callback obligation.
contracts.blocking: Asynchronous/non-blocking API, but takes internal locks/backend call; API-return order is not a callback fence.
contracts.return_codes: 0: submitted; BUSY: already submitted, so prior live cycle is not retired; NO_DEVICE/NOT_SUPPORTED/INVALID_PARAM/other errors require per-cycle reconciliation.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Success path unlocks transfer at io.c1562 before public return at1570. Another event thread can acquire transfer lock and invoke callback before that return; callback may free transfer. Success tail uses local r and does not dereference transfer.
conditions: Pre-register operation/session/submission cycle before native call.
Hold separate adapter operation-state reference for the whole submit call; reconcile return exactly once without assuming callback has not already run.
Do not access a raw transfer after return if callback ownership may already have freed it.
Do not hold an adapter mutex across submit if callback needs it and the chosen implementation would wait cyclically.
limitations: Source-permitted interleaving, not native reproduction, timing frequency or universal backend promise.
Failed attempt is not interchangeable with a known unsubmitted fresh transfer: BUSY explicitly denotes existing submission.
Library permitting callback-side free is not itself a libusb memory-safety defect.
contracts.conclusion: With successful submit, independent event thread and already-arrived completion, callback-before-public-submit-return is a valid source-level interleaving.

contracts.owner: Exactly one transfer-free owner; buffer-free flags and application-owned user_data have separate ownership.
contracts.blocking: Free has no drain/wait semantics; callback executes in whichever thread handles events.
contracts.return_codes: void; no success receipt proving associated application buffers drained.
contracts.callback_last_reference: libusb allows free inside terminal callback. With FREE_TRANSFER flag libusb frees after callback returns; manually freeing there as well is invalid. Adapter may intentionally defer free until its own call/callback references reach zero.
conditions: Do not free active submitted transfer.
Select automatic or manual transfer-free ownership, not both.
Protect user_data/session/pixel copies independently of the raw transfer object.
If deferring free until all adapter stack borrows return, disable conflicting auto-free ownership and account for internal libuvc-owned transfers.
limitations: The protocol-model callback_exit->free ordering is a conservative adapter design, not a universal libusb requirement.
Cannot implement a private libuvc transfer ownership change solely by assuming public handles expose those transfers.

contains: not legal to free an active transfer
Do not call this function with the usbi_transfer lock held

contracts.conclusion: New distinction: physical transfer deallocation may occur inside callback; application last-reference accounting is broader and remains mandatory.

contracts.owner: Caller borrows a still-live transfer throughout cancel call; completion callback and operation state retain separate obligations.
contracts.blocking: Asynchronous cancellation request; internally locks transfer. Return is not cancellation completion.
contracts.return_codes: 0: cancellation request successful; NOT_FOUND: not in progress/already complete/already cancelling; other LIBUSB_ERROR may occur.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Completion clears IN_FLIGHT before invoking callback, so NOT_FOUND does not establish callback exit. Repeated cancel can also see CANCELLING. After cancel unlock, callback may run/free before public cancel return.
conditions: Keep explicit cancel-call reference or equivalent synchronisation; do not start cancel on retired transfer.
NOT_FOUND/NO_DEVICE/error must not remove completion or callback obligations.
A delayed result notification may be identity-only only if the native call has already ended and no pointer is retained.
limitations: No API returns an all-callbacks-drained receipt.
Do not convert wrapper timeout or cancellation Future into native completion.
contracts.conclusion: New precision: NOT_FOUND can precede callback entry/exit, and cancel-call return itself is a separate last-reference boundary.

contracts.signature: int LIBUSB_CALL libusb_control_transfer(libusb_device_handle *dev_handle, uint8_t bmRequestType, uint8_t bRequest, uint16_t wValue, uint16_t wIndex, unsigned char *data, uint16_t wLength, unsigned int timeout);
contracts.owner: Caller keeps handle/data/own call state alive through return. Internal transfer/buffer and stack completed flag are owned by synchronous implementation.
contracts.blocking: Blocking; timeout=0 means unlimited. Internally submits asynchronous transfer and handles/waits for events.
contracts.return_codes: Nonnegative byte count on success; TIMEOUT/PIPE/NO_DEVICE/BUSY/INVALID_PARAM/NO_MEM/OVERFLOW/IO/OTHER errors possible.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Internal sync callback sets completed and must stop accessing transfer; submitting thread later reads result and frees transfer. Other callbacks may run on synchronous-call thread because it participates in event handling.
conditions: Hold blocking-call reference until function truly returns, regardless of caller deadline.
Do not call synchronous libusb API from event handling callback; implementation returns BUSY.
Do not use close as an authorised substitute for cancellation/return.
Keep own event-thread assumptions compatible with synchronous API doing event handling.
limitations: sync wait loop contains a dev_handle==NULL fallback after close, but that is not a public concurrency/lifetime guarantee.
No public handle for cancelling this internally allocated transfer is returned to caller.

contains: another thread might free the transfer
synchronous I/O functions you call from other threads

contracts.conclusion: New precision: requester timeout is not synchronous-call return; pump callbacks are not confined to the designated pump thread when synchronous APIs are also used.

contracts.owner: Caller owns devh/ctrl lifetime for full probe call; libuvc uses internal stack control payload.
contracts.blocking: Two synchronous USB control operations, internal timeout=0; no outer bounded guarantee.
contracts.return_codes: Implementation returns INVALID_MODE if parameter comparison fails, otherwise SUCCESS; SET/GET return codes are not propagated here.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Keep probe/open-control call reference until actual return; it is not a separately exposed asynchronous request.
conditions: Do not treat UVC_SUCCESS alone as proof both control exchanges succeeded.
Resolve finite/control cancellation and error-propagation contract before implementing real adapter.
limitations: Previously identified upstream gap remains unpatched.
No model result closes this native API gap.
contracts.conclusion: Inherited blocking/error propagation gap retained without re-running protocol model.

contracts.owner: Pump/calling thread borrows context, timeval and optional completed integer until return; callback user_data has its own lifetime.
contracts.blocking: tv bounds waiting for events, not total time executing callback/user code or all contention. Zero timeval polls pending events but can still execute callbacks.
contracts.return_codes: 0: event handling/wait successful, including ordinary timeout/no drain; INVALID_PARAM for invalid timeval; other LIBUSB_ERROR on failure.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Callbacks run in event-handling context; completed checked after event lock, or waiters lock path. completed must be updated under the library event lock as documented, typically in callback.
conditions: Do not interpret 0 or elapsed tv as all work drained.
Keep context alive until all pump/synchronous event-handler calls have returned.
If using completed, honour its library locking/lifetime rules; do not pass an unsynchronised stop bool as int pointer.
Keep event processing alive for cancel completions until independently counted obligations reach zero.
limitations: A finite poll interval cannot preempt a callback blocked in application code.
Event-loop return is not an application/native full-drain receipt.

contains: must be modified while holding the event lock
maximum time to block waiting for events

contracts.conclusion: New precision: finite pump wait and completed race protection must not be confused with bounded callback duration or drain.

contracts.owner: Caller borrows live context while signalling; pump thread remains owned and joinable by adapter.
contracts.blocking: Signals event source under event-data lock; does not cancel transfers, join thread or preempt running callback.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Event-handler processing clears USER_INTERRUPT; adapter must observe its own stop condition and actually return/join.
conditions: After transfer/callback obligations and non-pump business native calls are drained, request pump exit and interrupt its wait. The pump event-handler stack and context borrow remain live until actual return/join; keep context valid throughout and call libusb_exit only after join.
Do not stop pumping merely because stop or cancel was requested.
limitations: No proof of a hard latency bound or callback interruption.
No guarantee interrupt makes a pending synchronous transfer return.
contracts.conclusion: New precision: interrupt is a wakeup mechanism, not cancellation/drain/termination.

contracts.owner: Exactly one wrapper-handle owner closes after transfer/callback/all native call references are quiescent. Original wrapped fd stays externally owned.
contracts.blocking: Documented non-blocking/no bus requests; implementation can acquire/wait on event handling lock. No hard latency proof.
contracts.return_codes: void; NULL is accepted, but repeat-close of a non-NULL freed pointer is not idempotent.
contracts.callback_last_reference: do_close removes in-flight records and clears dev_handle; it does not wait for cancellation callback completion. It warns on unfinished transfer.
conditions: Use owner-level idempotency, not repeated native close of same pointer.
Prove status/image/control and submit/cancel/open/control call references drained before handle release.
Do not hold a lock needed by event callbacks while waiting for libusb_close event lock.
limitations: Source contains defensive handling of unfinished transfers, not permission to use close as cancellation barrier.
Library handle close does not close borrowed Android fd.

contains: A cancellation hasn't even been scheduled

contracts.conclusion: New precision: close acquires library event lock but is not an all-transfer drain or a wrapper-level idempotency primitive.

contracts.owner: libuvc owns stream transfers/callback thread/buffers; adapter must keep event pumping and its own callback work alive until return.
contracts.blocking: Stop cancels then unbounded cond_wait and callback pthread_join; close can invoke stop then release/free buffers.
contracts.return_codes: stop: INVALID_PARAM when not running, otherwise SUCCESS after waits; close: void.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Stop waits until transfer slots cleared and user callback thread joined; this excludes separate status transfer and adapter/Java queues.
conditions: Do not call stop synchronously from the same user callback thread.
Maintain event pump for cancellations.
Use broader status/control/all-call references and Java ownership conditions for full drain.
limitations: No timeout; source camera-side stop TODO remains.
Not a whole-device or full-pixel-drain receipt.

contracts.owner: libuvc frees UVC device handle and internal libusb handle; external fd/context owner retained when context borrowed.
contracts.blocking: May stop/join stream; borrowed context event thread is not joined; no contractual bound.
contracts.return_codes: void; cannot report a rich all-obligation completion result.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Status callback resubmits, but close path lacks explicit status cancel/wait and free_devh frees status_xfer.
conditions: Status lifecycle gap must be fixed or otherwise proven closed before actual integration.
Do not use public stream stop as proof status/call references are drained.
Do not close/release borrowed context or fd while uvc_close itself is on stack.
limitations: Static inherited blocker, not a reproduced exploit/native fault.
No safe product stop receipt follows merely from calling this unmodified function.
contracts.conclusion: Inherited status cancellation/drain blocker remains a precondition, not solved by the new interface document.

contracts.owner: libuvc frees its UVC context; only destroys USB context when own_usb_ctx is true. Adapter remains owner of a supplied USB context/pump.
contracts.blocking: Calls uvc_close for remaining devices; can inherit its waits; no hard bound.
contracts.return_codes: void; not idempotent for same freed context pointer.
contracts.callback_last_reference: All references to UVC context/devices become invalid; borrowed USB context still alive until owner later exits it.
conditions: Prefer explicit tracked device closure before UVC context teardown.
Require no concurrent UVC API calls before freeing context.
Keep borrowed USB context/pump alive through any needed close/cancel work.
limitations: Does not free Java copies or prove application full drain.
Single active-device route only; this is not a multi-device iteration/concurrency audit.
contracts.conclusion: New precision: uvc_exit is not ownership transfer of a borrowed USB context and cannot substitute for pump join.

contracts.owner: Dedicated-context owner alone destroys context after devices closed and all context users/event threads returned.
contracts.blocking: Teardown/locks; no caller deadline or thread-join guarantee.
contracts.return_codes: void; explicit context must not be reused after free.
contracts.callback_last_reference: Implementation explicitly assumes nobody accesses context during final unlocked teardown.
conditions: Close devices first.
Interrupt and join dedicated pump after obligations drain, and wait every synchronous/native context borrower.
Only then call libusb_exit; separately close external original FD owner after its native users finish.
limitations: Does not wait for a caller-created pump thread to exit.
Open-device warning and remaining-device handling are not a safe-cleanup protocol.

contains: nobody will be accessing the context

contracts.conclusion: New precision: context teardown assumes quiescence; the adapter must establish it before exit.

validation.verification: all selected bytes, size and Git blob match inherited tracked lock; every exact anchor is within its recorded line range

open_boundaries: No native reproduction of callback-before-public-return; source-level permitted schedule only.
No proof of finite open/submit/cancel/close/callback execution latency.
Unmodified libuvc status teardown and probe error/timeout gaps remain.
Adapter reference counting, lock order, JNI ownership and failure cleanup not implemented here.
Native drain is separate from Java/pixel full drain; product gate remains external.
